column3: “Lifted up of face” is rendered “highly respected,” and “having a skin disease” as “a leper.”
“She was before” is rendered “she waited on.”
“Deliver him from his skin disease” is rendered “cure him of his leprosy.”
The Hebrew says “he went”; NASB names “Naaman” and adds “in.”
NASB supplies “shekels.”
“Deliver” is rendered “cure,” and “skin disease” as “leprosy.”
“Seeking an opportunity” is rendered “seeking a quarrel.”
NASB supplies “word.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Angry” is rendered “furious,” and “I said to myself” as “I thought.” “The one having a skin disease” is rendered “the leper.”
The written Hebrew reads “Abanah” (reading tradition “Amana”); NASB has “Abanah.” “Good” is rendered “better.”
The Hebrew אָבִי (“would that,” often read “my father”) is rendered “My father.”
“A young lad” is rendered “a little child.”
“Camp” is rendered “company,” and “blessing” as “present.”
The oath form “if I will accept” is rendered “I will take nothing.”
“And not” is rendered “If not,” and NASB adds “at least.”
“Bow down” is rendered “worship” and “bow myself.”
“A distance of land” is rendered “some distance.”
“He said” is rendered “thought,” and “restrained” as “spared.”
“Fell from the chariot” is rendered “came down from the chariot.”
“Peace” is rendered “All is well.”
“Be willing” is rendered “Be pleased.”
“The hill” translates the Hebrew הָעֹפֶל (Ophel).
“Where and where” is rendered “nowhere.”
NASB supplies “with you.”
NASB adds “Therefore,” and renders “having a skin disease like snow” as “a leper as white as snow.”
